text:
Public service broadcasters’ streaming services such as BBC iPlayer should appear first on app menus on smart TVs to give them an “appropriate degree of prominence”, according to Ofcom.
In addition, the regulator has said public service shows should rank higher on voice and text searches on televisions connected to the internet.
In an increasingly fragmented media world, TV guides and app menus act as gatekeepers to content and vary according to which set viewers have, with users often having to scroll for some time to find the traditional broadcasters.
So as part of the 2024 Media Act – which modernised the framework for making public service broadcasting content easier to discover on connected TVs – Ofcom has announced a new code of practice that it hopes will help audiences locate PSB shows more easily and standardise prominence on TV screens.
The code includes ensuring that the PSB’s streaming services “should be immediately visible” and “appear with the first nine” app icons or “tiles” on smart TV main app menus.
Ofcom said they should appear “in the following order … BBC iPlayer, ITVX, Channel 4 player, Channel 5 player, S4C Clic and STV player”, with the positioning changing depending on where the user is in the UK.
The regulator added that when searching for shows (including voice searches) via connected TVs, “public service programmes should be more prominent than other programmes where they are the most relevant results for a user’s search”.
Other recommendations include “public service programmes should be clearly attributed to the designated PSB service in which they are included” so it “helps audiences identify the content provider and make informed viewing choices”, and improving the “experience of disabled people” through labelling and enabling accessibility features such as subtitles or audio description.
Although the code is not mandatory, Ofcom hopes its recommendations could be in place within the next 12 to 18 months and said platform providers that follow it “will be treated as complying with the relevant prominence and accessibility duties”.
This issue is separate to that of greater prominence for established broadcasters and media companies on digital platforms such as YouTube and TikTok, the debate over which is continuing.
PSBs have argued that their content should be safeguarded to protect the “shared social fabric of the UK”, and the government published plans this summer saying they could be given more prominence on the algorithmically driven platforms owned by the big tech and social media companies.
However, some media companies and content creators have argued against more visibility for PSBs on YouTube and TikTok, maintaining it will adversely affect their businesses.
digest_he:
רשות הרגולציה של התקשורת בבריטניה, Ofcom, פרסמה קוד פרקטיקה חדש שנועד להבטיח לשירותי הסטרימינג של גופי השידור הציבורי נראות ובולטות גבוהה במסכי הטלוויזיה החכמה. על פי ההנחיות החדשות, אפליקציות כמו BBC iPlayer, ITVX ושירותים מקבילים נוספים צריכים להופיע מיד בתפריטים הראשיים ובתוך תשעת סמלי האפליקציות הראשונים במסכי הטלוויזיה.

בנוסף, הרגולטור קבע כי תוכניות של שידור ציבורי צריך לקבל עדיפות גבוהה יותר בתוצאות חיפוש קוליות ומבוססות טקסט בטלוויזיות המחוברות לאינטרנט. המהלך נועד לסייע לצופים לאתר תוכן איכותי בקלות בעולם מדיה מפוצל, ולספק גישה נוחה יותר גם למאפייני נגישות כמו כתוביות. הרגולציה אינה מחויבת באופן מידי, אך הרשות מקווה שפלטפורמות השידור יישמו את ההמלצות בחודשים הקרובים.
